title: Per-route quota inheritance bug causes retroactive billing adjustments during canary policy merges
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Summary: During a staged canary rollout of a hierarchical per-route quota inheritance change, we observed retroactive adjustments to previously-reported usage for affected tenants. Some keys were granted positive credit adjustments after policy merge boundaries, causing underbilling for a subset of traffic. The issue appears tied to policy merge ordering + asynchronous policy application + reservation accounting when a route changes its effective parent during a window boundary.

Context: We introduced a change to allow route-level quotas to inherit and override parent pool credits with a more permissive merge behavior (intended to ease transitions). The rollout is a canary that patches policy propagation and the policy-merge code path. On canary traffic we saw unexpected decreases in billed token counts and a handful of orgs received retroactive credit allocations in the daily aggregate.

Why this is critical: This impacts accounting correctness (billing and quota enforcement), can allow transient over-allow, and breaks guarantees for Dedicated customers who expect deterministic per-route spend.
repro_steps: Deploy the canary policy merge on edge shard A with policy-version V+1 while shard B remains on V
Create a parent route (R_parent) with remaining credits, and a child route (R_child) that was recently remapped from a different pool
Send a steady traffic stream from the same API key that exercises R_child across the epoch boundary (close to top-of-window), ensuring some requests get evaluated under V and some under V+1
Observe enforcement logs, per-key reservation records, and the reconciler run that applies merged policy deltas
Check final daily aggregate for that org and compare to pre-change snapshots — look for positive credit corrections and missing debits
observed_metrics_and_logs: spike in reconciler.adjustment_count: +320 in the 10m window after deploy
per-key reservation table shows two entries for same transaction id with conflicting policy_version
billing-aggregator reported -0.7% delta for affected orgs compared to expected baseline
enforcer logs: "policy-merge applied with no-op for existing reservation id", followed by "applied_credit_delta: +X tokens"
trace: policy-sync (v1.20) latency increased from 12ms -> 180ms during rollout window
investigation_notes: Preliminary root cause: when a policy merge changes inheritance for a route, the policy-engine re-evaluates existing reservations atomically in-memory but writes reconciler adjustments asynchronously. If the enforcer services on different shards reconcile the same reservation against different policy snapshots (old vs new) there is a window where the final write path applies the delta using the newer snapshot without compensating for prior debits.

Edge case: transactions that were partially served (KV cache present) have memoized per-token debit counts. The reconciler applies the merged policy delta as if those tokens had never been debited under the old policy, resulting in a net positive credit in the aggregator.

Race appears amplified by: (1) policy-sync backoff retry causing duplicate adjust attempts, (2) reconciler idempotency key generation changed in runtime-1.20 causing mismatches, (3) cross-shard lease migration during canary causing mixed policy views.
interim_mitigations: Pause canary rollout immediately and revert the policy merge change on the affected shards (done: rolled shards A,B back at 2026-03-10 09:22 UTC)
Enable strict policy-version pinning for enforcer until we ship a reconciliation fix (config flag: enforce_policy_versioned_reservations=true)

Run a targeted backfill that computes reconciliation deltas and emits compensating metering events to re-align billing aggregates for impacted orgs (backfill PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/432)
Notify CS and Billing with a summary and action plan (message posted to #billing-incidents)
proposed_fix: 1) Introduce epoched policy snapshots: reservations must reference the policy_epoch they were evaluated under. 2) Make reconciler adjustments compute delta = current_policy.compute_adj(reservation_state) - reservation_state.applied_under_epoch to avoid double counting. 3) Strengthen idempotency keys for adjustments using (reservation_id, policy_epoch). 4) Add cross-shard guard: a lightweight lease check that prevents two shards reconciling the same reservation concurrently. 5) Add unit/integration tests simulating interleaved policy-sync and canary traffic.
implementation_tasks: ENG: add policy_epoch to reservation protobuf and database column (migrate with default=0)
ENG: update reconciler to include policy_epoch in idempotency key and calculation path
ENG: add cross-shard reconcile guard based on existing shard-lease API
ENG: add end-to-end tests simulating policy merge and route remap across epoch boundary
OPS: run backfill script and validate aggregates against pre-deploy snapshot
SWEET: run canary with sysbench traffic and monitor reconciler.adjustment_count metric
rollback_plan: If after fix we still observe (>0.1%) underbilling: revert policy_epoch gating and restore previous deterministic policy-merge behavior; run full double-check reconciliation across all shards and trigger manual audit for any orgs with >$100 discrepancy.
comments: 2026-03-08 Sofia Ramirez: Logged after CS flagged a downstream billing variance for 3 enterprise orgs. Attached initial logs and aggregator snapshot.
2026-03-09 Ethan Brooks: Reproduced locally with a two-shard cluster; confirmed dual-apply of adjustments due to idempotency key mismatch. Beginning design for policy_epoch approach.
2026-03-10 Priya Shah (SRE): Paused canary and reverted deploy on shards A and B. Running the backfill dry-run against staging aggregates.
2026-03-11 Marcus Lee (Billing): Executed targeted backfill on staging, deltas within expected bounds. Requested a second opinion from finance for production backfill timing.

2026-03-12 Ethan Brooks: Started implemention branch runtime#1894, added reservation.policy_epoch field and updated reconciler idempotency; unit tests added. Needs review from infra and billing teams.
2026-03-12 Aisha Patel (PM): Marked P0 due to customer impact and asked for daily status updates until completion.
acceptance_criteria: All reservations persisted with policy_epoch; reconciler idempotency prevents double adjustment across policy changes
E2E test reproducing old failure returns identical billed totals before and after policy merge
Canary run for 48 hours shows reconciler.adjustment_count within historical baseline and no retroactive positive credits observed
Billing team signs off on backfill results and produces a reconciled report for impacted orgs
next_steps: Code review for runtime#1894 and ops#432 (assigned: infra + billing)
Schedule production backfill window with Finance & Customer Success for low-traffic period
Add monitoring alert to detect policy_epoch divergence (>0) between shards within a 30s window
Ship runtime-1.20.1 with the patch and gated rollout behind enforce_policy_versioned_reservations flag
